why: PRINCIPLES 7, for seniority. The claim every plugin host makes is that its `schema.json` plus its README is enough for an agent to write a working plugin in one turn, and that `seniority check` tells it so without a human reading the output. Until 2026-09-22 only flagstaff measured that; this is seniority's half. If the agent needs a second turn, or someone has to explain a refusal, the schema is not self-describing and `check` is not the feedback loop it claims to be.
prompt: Read packages/seniority/src/schema.json and packages/seniority/README.md. Write a seniority plugin to the file evals/results/vault-plugin.mjs. It must be a single ES module with a default export, must be named "vault", and must contribute one configuration source called "vault" that ranks above the config file and below the environment. Then verify it by running: node packages/seniority/dist/cli.js check evals/results/vault-plugin.mjs — and if that command exits non-zero, fix the plugin until it exits zero. Do not modify anything under packages/.

expect.value: node packages/seniority/dist/cli.js check evals/results/vault-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^vault: ok'
node packages/seniority/dist/cli.js check evals/results/vault-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^vault — 1 sources'
